sections.title: 1. Property A (95014) — carrying costs today
sections.intro: Owner-supplied amounts are marked 'owner'. Anything that could be checked against a published tariff is marked 'verified' or 'derived'.

rows.note: Owner range $100–$150/month. Cross-check below.

rows.value: ≈ $110–$130/month for 10–12 Ccf plus the meter service charge
rows.note: Tier 1 (0–6 Ccf) $4.97–$5.04, Tier 2 (6–12 Ccf) $7.42–$7.52 per Ccf. 12 Ccf ≈ $75 of volume plus a fixed service charge. The owner's range is consistent with the tariff — no discrepancy.
Consistent with legacy net metering; see the solar section for why this may not survive to 2045+.

sections.title: 3. Insurance — the least verifiable, most under-estimated line
sections.intro: No public dataset prices a specific high-value Bay Area house. Rather than invent a premium, the model prices insurance as a rate on replacement cost and shows the sensitivity. Both owner figures look low for these building values.

rows.note: Equal to the premium a ~$300,000 dwelling typically carries. Property A's structure alone is worth well over $1,000,000.

rows.value: 0.30% of replacement cost per year, escalated 6%/yr, capped at 0.80%
rows.note: Property A: ≈$5,120/yr in 2026. Property B (landlord policy, ×1.4): ≈$4,160/yr. Range tested in sensitivity.
Coastal California split for a 1960s–70s tract house. Needs a replacement-cost estimator (F-07).

rows.item: Why the model is above the owner's figure
rows.value: A $3.1M house with a $1.7M replacement cost is not priced like a $300k house
rows.note: California premiums rose sharply 2023–2026 and many carriers now require a FAIR Plan wrap for high-value or fire-exposed homes. If the actual policy is genuinely $1,500, the model overstates costs by ≈$3,600/yr — not enough to change the ranking of options.
A separate CEA policy on a $1.7M structure typically runs four figures per year. Unpriced here — flagged F-11.

rows.item: San Jose Water Company Tier 1 / 2 / 3 quantity rates
rows.note: Two CPUC-approved tariff filings in 2026 carry slightly different effective dates; both shown. Historical increases ≈4–5%/yr, which is the growth rate used (A4).
Tier 1 applies to the first 3 Ccf per dwelling per month.
Tariff values reported from PG&E's published E-1 schedule; the PDF itself could not be retrieved from this sandbox (F-12). Electricity is a small line for both properties.

rows.value: 20-year term tied to the system and inherited by a buyer
rows.note: 'The 20-year NEM legacy program rules are tied to the system, not the owner.'

rows.value: applies to interconnections applied for after 14 April 2023
rows.note: Export credits are far below retail, so a post-legacy solar house pays materially more for evening/night power.

rows.value_display: likely no longer a net-zero bill
rows.note: If the system was interconnected before 2023, the 20-year legacy term ends by 2043 at the latest. The model therefore assumes an electricity cost from transfer year +16 onward (A29). This directly contradicts the owner's 'no electricity cost' expectation for the post-inheritance period.
